newsitem.title: GERMANY: North German beet study shows mixed results.
newsitem.headline: North German beet study shows mixed results.

text.p: Sample sugar beet taken from northern German fields last week showed a lower beet weight but a higher sugar content than last year, data from key producer Zuckerverbund Nord AG (ZVN) showed.
The industry test put beet weight per hectare in the north at 54.8 tonnes per hectare compared with 63.5 in 1995, but average sugar content at 16.70 percent, up from 16.00 a year earlier.
The implied sugar yield was 9.16 tonnes per hectare (10.20 in 1995).
The number of beet per hectare, at 86,709, exceeded last year's 78,900.
ZVN operates seven factories and is the second largest German sugar producer.
The sugarbeet campaign will start in some southern regions this week.

Traders said the northern indications showed recent rainfall was beneficial, although the crop had suffered from drought in the winter. They were keenly awaiting the fourth national beet test results, which will be issued on Monday afternoon.
